old_caption: The video showcases a series of colorful dominoes arranged in intricate patterns on a wooden floor. The dominoes are organized into distinct sections, each featuring a different color: red, blue, yellow, orange, and green. These colors are arranged in a way that creates a visually appealing design. The camera remains static, capturing the detailed arrangement and the vibrant hues of the dominoes. The background includes a radiator and a wall outlet, indicating an indoor setting. The overall atmosphere is one of creativity and precision, as the viewer is drawn into the intricate details of the domino arrangement.
original_wisa_caption: The video showcases a series of colorful dominoes arranged in intricate patterns on a wooden floor. The dominoes are organized into distinct sections, each featuring a different color: red, blue, yellow, orange, green, and purple. These colors are arranged in a way that creates a visually appealing and symmetrical design. The camera pans slowly across the scene, highlighting the detailed arrangement and the vibrant hues of the dominoes. As the camera moves, it captures the smooth transitions between the different colored sections, emphasizing the meticulous planning behind the setup. The background includes a radiator and a wall outlet, indicating an indoor setting. The overall atmosphere is one of creativity and precision, as the viewer is drawn into the intricate details of the domino arrangement.
caption: The video showcases an angled overhead view of a floor covered with serpentine chains of standing plastic dominoes, sorted by color. Red and blue chains coil across a lighter wooden section at the left, while yellow and orange chains spread over a darker floor. A white radiator and a small outlet line the top wall, with a green loop at the far left edge. Throughout the excerpt the chains remain upright and unchanged, with no toppling or chain reaction visible. A few pieces, including a flat pinkish-orange domino in the bottom loop, are already down and stay so. The only motion is a slow drift of the framing, as the outlet and radiator slide left and the edge loops partly leave view. This gradual shift reflects a steady camera pan rather than any movement of the dominoes.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.

and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.

Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
